html:
An Australian mining company founded in 1885 as the Broken Hill Proprietary Company, to mine silver, lead and zinc at Broken Hill in western New South Wales. It grew into one of the largest mining companies in the world.

A boundary rider, Charles Rasp, pegged the claim in 1883, thinking the ridge held tin. It turned out to sit on one of the richest silver, lead and zinc deposits ever found. Broken Hill became a hard mining town with fierce strikes, and the company grew rich. In 1915 it opened a steelworks at Newcastle, and for most of the 20th century it was Australia's biggest company and its steel maker.

Later it moved into oil, coal, copper and iron ore, above all in the Pilbara of Western Australia, much of it shipped to China. In 2001 it merged with the Anglo Dutch firm Billiton, and it is now based in Melbourne. In 2015 a dam at a Brazilian mine it co-owned with Vale collapsed, in the Mariana dam disaster. See Australia and the gold rush that began Australia's mining age.
